newsitem.title: UK: London Int'l says new condom works.
newsitem.headline: London Int'l says new condom works.

text.p: A new condom made of polyurethane instead of latex works just as well, makers London International Group Plc said on Monday.
LIG, one of the world's biggest makers of condoms, said a U.S. study just finished showed the Durex Avanti did not break any more often than latex condoms.
The Durex Avanti, which will be marketed in Britain in the autumn, is targeted at people with a sensitivity to latex.
"It is transparent, odourless and safe to use with oil-and water-based lubricants," William Potter, scientific affairs director for London International, said in a statement.
A study carried out by the Los Angeles Regional Family Planning Council using more than 800 volunteer couples, found the new condom broke four percent of the time, the statement said.
A study published last spring found latex condoms broke, slipped or otherwise failed five percent of the time.
"This is one of the most comprehensive studies ever undertaken for condoms," Ron Frezieres, director of research for the council, said in the statement.
"We are pleased with the results, which have established the contraceptive efficacy of both Durex Avanti and Durex Ramses latex condoms."
The condoms are sold in the U.S. now without a prevention of pregnancy claim on the label, pending approval from the Food and Drug Administration.
"Durex Avanti already has approval for launch in Europe and we have every confidence that it will shortly receive full clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration," Potter said.
The company said Avanti was made from Duron, a specially developed polyurethane, which it said had double the strength of latex.
It said the new condoms, which will be sold at a higher price than latex condoms, were thinner and better able to conduct body heat.

The company told Reuters the response of British trade buyers to the new condom had exceeded expectations, with leading pharmacy chains Boots Co Plc BOOT.L and Superdrug signed up to sell it at all their stores in the autumn.
"The trade response so far has surpassed all expectations," LIG said.
